transcript: Just in time for pride. Here comes la cage aux folles at New York City Center, Encores! I was at invited dress rehearsal last night, and as always, I'm going to tell you all about it. But as this was a dress rehearsal, this is not going to be a review per se, as much as a high level what to expect. this is the first time that this show has ever been done with an all black cast. And while La Cage has always been a Celebration of queer joy, this production specifically celebrates black queer joy. And I think that is so important right now. And in many ways, this show has never felt more timely. I mean, the antagonist of the piece is literally a politician that wants to villainize queer people and performers, specifically drag performers. And so having a show that defiantly stands against that mentality very much feels like using art as a form of political protest. And on top of that, an incredibly solid production LED by Billy Porter and Wayne Brady, and you have a show that feels like it is ready to go to Broadway tomorrow. As similar to most recent encores! Shows, despite the fact that this is technically a concert production and the entire thing is put together with very little rehearsal time, there is full choreography, a simple but sufficient set, and nary a binder in sight. In fact, I think the only two performers I saw with binders on stage, Were Billy and Wayne, and even then they weren't overly reliant on them. It was mostly there as a safety net. And especially Wayne. I don't think even looked at his binder once. And I will admit I was a big doubter of Billy Porter when his casting was announced. I really have not loved a lot of his recent stage work, but I am thrilled to say that he is excellent here and really won me over. And he is perfectly paired with Wayne Brady, who is just once again doing sensational work. This really does feel like the most transfer ready Encores! production that they've done in a while, and so I would definitely not be surprised to see this come to Broadway, especially with how perfectly timed this whole production feels. But nothing is guaranteed, so if you wanna see this production I highly recommend getting to City Center in the next two weeks. I really don't think you'll be disappointed.
